items.title: Macmillan Staff Say the Publisher Threw a Party for a Workplace AI Assistant That Was Later Killed
items.excerpt: Workers tell WIRED that Macmillan's internal assistant NOA ('No Ordinary Assistant') was unhelpful before it was shut down. Bestselling authors also say AI is ruining their relationships with Big Five publishers.

items.title: 'There is no inevitable dystopia': Jeanette Winterson on AI and the future of humanity
items.excerpt: The novelist argues that humanity is at a turning point as a species and that an AI future is not fated to be dystopian, setting out how writers and readers should approach the technology.

items.title: AI 시대 출판업계, 위기냐 기회냐…亞 출판인 한자리에
items.excerpt: 한국출판인회의가 11월 3~6일 '2026 아시아 출판 주간'을 열고, 대만·베트남·싱가포르·독일 등 7개 지역 출판인 11명과 함께 AI 시대 출판업계의 위기와 기회, AI·저작권 문제를 논의한다.

items.title: Who Keeps the Catalog of Connectors? The Coming MCP Discovery Problem
items.excerpt: As AI agents reach scholarly content through MCP connectors, the piece argues libraries and vendors need to build registries and metadata feeds so those connectors can be found, accessed and used.

items.title: Pulitzer Prize-Winner's Newest Work is AI Generated
items.excerpt: The gold-and-white sticker on the cover of the 25th-anniversary edition of Art Spiegelman's graphic novel In the Shadow of No Towers was AI-generated, as Spiegelman told Publishers Weekly in an interview.

history_match.title: Caine Prize initiates ‘human-centred process’ after Zimbabwean winner accused of AI use

items.title: Anthropic illegally trained Claude with Stanford professors' books
items.excerpt: Books by at least 10 Stanford academics appear among the pirated works covered by Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement. The professors are now asking what the training use means for their scholarship.

history_match.title: Authors Guild Calls on Publishers to Share Anthropic Wealth

items.title: Escritor peruano es acusado de presentar obra con 99% de IA a concurso donde ganó un premio de 20.000 euros
items.excerpt: A Pangram scan run by El País attributed 99% of David Silva Rojas's prize-winning novel 'Donde el agua trabaja' to AI. The author denies it, and publisher Almadía has cancelled launch events and opened a review.

items.title: News Podcast: Audible Lets Listeners Talk to Dracula; Plaintiffs Drop a Key AI Study Against OpenAI
items.excerpt: Dan Holloway covers Audible's new AI feature that lets listeners converse with Dracula from its audio adaptation, alongside SelfPubCon takeaways and the Books by People human-authorship label.

history_match.title: Audible's new features let you explore book worlds — and use AI to talk to characters

items.title: AI is Already Everywhere in Publishing
items.excerpt: Book Riot's podcast discusses a so-called exposé of how the publishing industry already uses AI, and yet another prize-winning story that appears to have been AI-written.

items.title: Can AI Run Your Book Marketing? Member Q&A with Michael La Ronn and Sacha Black
items.excerpt: Michael La Ronn and Sacha Black assess how far indie authors can hand book marketing to AI tools, covering ads, copy and campaign workflows, alongside other member questions.

items.title: The detection wars: AI is publishing's 'wicked problem'
items.excerpt: ALLi director Orna Ross examines how AI detection tools are being used to cancel books and authors. She argues that due process matters more than certifying writing as 'human-made'.

history_match.title: Pangram CEO says ‘no bias’ in its AI-detection tool, as adoption rises

items.title: Why Are Publishers Suing Big Tech With One Hand and Embracing AI With the Other?
items.excerpt: Writing after an Authors Guild panel on authorship and AI, the essayist examines the contradiction of publishers that litigate against AI companies while adopting AI tools in their own workflows.
